Robot Doctor Sensors & odometry

IMU heading is wrong or field-centric is broken

Heading off by 90/180°, turns the wrong way, or resets. Below are the 4 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 5 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • When you turn the robot 90° left by hand, does heading read about +90? Reset yaw, turn left a quarter turn, read telemetry.
  • Does heading suddenly jump back to 0 during a match? Like the robot "forgets" where it was pointing.
  • Does your code use BNO055IMU instead of the newer IMU class? Search for "BNO055IMU".
  • When turning to a heading, does it sometimes spin almost a full circle the long way? Common when the target is near ±180°.
  • Does it happen right after touching a field wall, field element, or another robot? Think about the last few times. Was the robot touching something metal just before?

Common causes and how to fix them

1 IMU told the wrong hub orientation

The universal IMU needs to know which way the hub's logo and USB ports face. Wrong values give a heading that is off by 90/180° or turns the wrong way.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Look at how your Control Hub is really mounted: which way the REV logo faces and which way the USB ports face (left and right as seen from behind the robot).
  2. Put exactly those directions in RevHubOrientationOnRobot.
  3. Test: reset yaw, turn the robot 90° left by hand, and yaw should read about +90.
Universal IMU setup
IMU imu = hardwareMap.get(IMU.class, "imu");
imu.initialize(new IMU.Parameters(new RevHubOrientationOnRobot(
        RevHubOrientationOnRobot.LogoFacingDirection.UP,
        RevHubOrientationOnRobot.UsbFacingDirection.FORWARD)));
imu.resetYaw();

double heading = imu.getRobotYawPitchRollAngles().getYaw(AngleUnit.DEGREES);

Sources: FTC Docs · Universal IMU interface · REV · IMU

2 IMU reset mid-match

Static shocks or a battery dip can reset the IMU, so heading jumps back to 0 halfway through a match.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Update the Control Hub OS. Version 1.1.4 reduced these resets on BHI260AP hubs.
  2. Use the ESD fixes (grounding strap, USB 3.0 port, insulated electronics) and secure the battery.
  3. Add a driver button that re-zeros the IMU while the robot is lined up with the tile seams.
Driver re-zero button
if (gamepad1.options) {
    imu.resetYaw();   // line the robot up straight first
}

Sources: REV · IMU · FTC Docs · Managing ESD

3 Using the old BNO055 code on a newer hub

Control Hubs since Sept 2022 have a BHI260AP IMU, which the legacy BNO055IMU interface does not support. Expansion Hubs since Dec 2021 have no IMU at all.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Switch to the universal IMU interface (SDK 8.1+), which works with both chips.
  2. Use the IMU on the Control Hub, since newer Expansion Hubs do not have one.
  3. Let the configuration auto-detect the IMU type on I2C port 0.

Sources: REV · IMU · FTC Docs · Universal IMU interface

4 Heading error isn't wrapped

Heading jumps from +180° to -180°. If the error is not wrapped, the robot spins the long way around.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Normalize the heading error to -180..180 before feeding it to your controller.
Wrap the error
double error = AngleUnit.normalizeDegrees(targetHeading - currentHeading);

Sources: GM0 · Control loops
